summary: Eastern Brazil’s missing centuries now contain named villages, camps and burial places. Wooden house piles, pottery, hearths and human remains establish local episodes; graphite and a carved green-stone pendant reveal connections beyond the places where they were found. The 30 map records comprise 29 evidence entries and one linked route view of the Canaã pottery evidence. No new battle marker is assigned: the reviewed bone modifications and suspected injuries do not establish a securely dated conflict in this campaign.

held.title: Violence at Zé Espinho
held.reason: The possible ray-spine injury and disputed fracture context belong to a different individual from the dated burial. They cannot supply a dated conflict marker.

held.title: Pedra do Cachorro: cut and broken bones
held.reason: The excavators attribute the marks to treatment of the dead. The dated burial is included, but cause of death and participants are unknown.

held.title: Boca do Rio pendant source
held.reason: The pendant is included with the village. Mineral analysis supports a nonlocal material, but no specific quarry, seller, journey or direct Caribbean route is established.

held.title: Canaã graphite
held.reason: The proposed source connection is included as tentative. Jequié is the closest of the tested comparisons, while other deposits remain untested. A separate coated sherd supplies the approximate date context.

held.title: Rio Preto Oeste 1 chronology
held.reason: The actual hearths, pottery and urn are included under the excavators’ provisional fourteenth-century interpretation. Internally inconsistent sample ages and possible contamination prevent a more precise chronology.

held.title: Bananeiras chronology
held.reason: The bone record uses the modern reported 1500–1681 CE calibration. The older 1420–1510 and 1600–1620 alternatives remain in its review. Separate pottery-residue dates concern different objects.

held.title: Peruaçu and Abrigo do Malhador
held.reason: Maize and hearth studies offer promising local histories. The accessible chronology gives central calibrated ages or raw radiocarbon ages; full individual calibrated ranges still need to be traced.

held.title: Toca da Baixa dos Caboclos
held.reason: The earliest potentially overlapping sample has inconsistent calendar BP and CE columns. Later dated individuals are outside this campaign.

held.title: Guipe, Beliscão, Sauípe, Água Vermelha and Justino
held.reason: The checked sources provide raw radiocarbon measurements or broad phase assignments. Traceable calendar ranges are needed before these particular observations enter this timeline. This does not imply that the places were unoccupied.

held.title: Piúma, Usiminas and Pontinha
held.reason: Published late measurements need a calibration or reconciliation of differing published ranges. They remain source-check priorities.
